clue.text: Hoax involving income from fairground attraction

definitions.meaning: to hoax someone is to deceive or con them
read whimsically, the money taken at a fairground is what is taken for a go on one of its rides

explanation.surface: A con trick that involves the cash taken at a funfair ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into 'take' (takings, income) earned 'for a ride' at the fair; 'involving' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for deceiving or swindling someone is to lead them on in this way, so it matches a hoax.

clue.text: Old Dandy found lying about — under carpeting?

indicators.note: the dandy's word lies around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a toff is a well-dressed upper-class man, a dandy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old copy of The Dandy comic is found lying around, perhaps under the rug.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy is a British children's comic, but here it is just a fop. 'found' is a link. 'Carpeting' is a scolding, as being called on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carpeted is British slang for being reprimanded, so someone under carpeting has been reprimanded.

clue.text: Frustrated when expecting knees-up, steps in to create a stir

indicators.note: stirring the words mixes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: At a lively party, dancers step in to cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party; here it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept waiting anxiously for an outcome describes someone frustrated while they expect news.

clue.text: Fellow philosopher looking up love goddess

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A scholar and a thinker gaze upward at a goddess of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Monk artist's included

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual artist, plus the 's
put in means included

explanation.surface: A monk who paints has been admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the Russian mystic monk who held sway at the court of the last tsar.

clue.text: Overcharge man for moving

definitions.meaning: to swindle a customer by charging far too much
a chess piece, one of the men moved on the board, also called a castle

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to fleece or cheat, and the noun is a chess piece that moves in straight lines.

clue.text: Unequivocally blue conservatives

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down
the right is the conservative side of politics

explanation.surface: Tories who are clearly true blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservatives, a false trail: here it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something downright is saying it plainly and without any qualification.

clue.text: Admit mistake, unable to sit after six of the best?

parts.note: someone who cannot sit must stay upright on their feet
six of the best is a caning, an old school punishment, so the pupil has been put right

explanation.surface: A caned pupil cannot sit down and owns up to the error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six of the best' is six strokes of the cane, an old British school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede that one was wrong is the idiom of accepting correction, so it means admitting a mistake.

clue.text: Detachment of Marines boarding vessel — very small one

indicators.note: boarding a ship means getting inside it, so the letters go into the vessel
detachment means the two letters for the Marines come apart, so each boards separately

parts.note: a ship is a vessel
RM, the Royal Marines; here its R
RM, the Royal Marines; here its M

explanation.surface: A unit of marines climbs aboard a ship, a tiny one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detachment of' splits RM, the Royal Marines, so R and M board SHIP on either side of its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is an informal word for a very small person or thing.

clue.text: Fail, wanting drinks, to be heard

indicators.note: signals that the word for the drinks is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a cat laps milk: laps is a verb for drinks

explanation.surface: Someone fails because they lack anything to drink, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is just a link joining the definition to the wordplay; the verb 'drinks' is the word that sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall short or lapse is to fail, as with a lapsed membership or a lapse of concentration.

clue.text: Timer, best in set of samples

indicators.note: the word for best is placed inside the word for a set of samples

parts.note: a swatch is a set of fabric samples
top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: A clock judges which is the finest among a batch of fabric samples.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch is a hand-held device for timing races and the like, so it is a timer.

clue.text: Wild herb you finally found, roaming aimlessly around

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the other piece, enclosing it
moving aimlessly suggests letters wandering into a new order
the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A forager finds a wild herb while wandering around without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aimlessly' rearranges ROAMING to ORIGANM, and 'around' puts U, the last letter of 'you' (from 'finally'), inside it; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Origanum is the genus of wild marjoram and oregano, aromatic herbs that grow wild.

clue.text: Be about to manage industrial initiative in sultanate

indicators.note: the letters of Be go about, surrounding the rest

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: the initial letter of industrial

explanation.surface: A call to take charge of industrial enterprise in an oil-rich Asian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets B and E round RUN plus I, the first letter of 'industrial' picked by 'initiative'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the island of Borneo, ruled by its sultan.

clue.text: This film's premiere stirred up trouble, as badly directed trailer may do

definitions.text: as badly directed trailer may do

indicators.note: a premiere is a first showing, so the first letter of film's
stirred up suggests the letters being mixed into a new order

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: A film's first night caused trouble, likened to a trailer that swings about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred up' rearranges THIS plus F (the 'premiere' of 'film's') into FISHT; AIL follows. A trailer badly steered swings from side to side, like a fish's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: When a towed trailer sways from side to side behind a vehicle, it is said to fishtail.

clue.text: Type of drive where couple caress

parts.note: a couple is two
to stroke is to caress

explanation.surface: A lovers' road trip where the pair fondle each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is a link. The 'drive' is an engine type, not a trip in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-stroke engine is a kind of motor drive used in mopeds and lawnmowers.

clue.text: Where part of clutch appears to be broken

definitions.text: Where part of clutch appears to be broken

parts.words: Where part of clutch appears to be broken
parts.note: clutch suggests a car pedal, but it is a hen's batch of eggs; one of them sits in a small holder at breakfast, ready to have its top cracked

explanation.surface: A mechanic wonders where the car's clutch looks damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled egg, one of a clutch, is served in this little holder and broken open there.

clue.text: Name ship after Irishman

indicators.note: the ship comes after the word for name

parts.note: to dub is to name
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Christening a vessel after an Irish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Ireland's capital city is a Dubliner, so he is an Irishman.

clue.text: One exploiting rule of French spy

parts.note: de is French for of
to spy or spot something is to catch sight of it

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a French regulation about espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant who uses absolute power for their own ends is a despot.

clue.text: Sent' up Iron Lady, about to pretetrate slander?

indicators.note: the reversed metal symbol is about to go into, penetrating, the word for lady

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Satirising the Iron Lady, Margaret Thatcher, as if about to slander her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretetrate' is printed as such for 'penetrate', a slip in the paper. The Iron Lady was Margaret Thatcher, but here the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: To defame is to damage a reputation with false statements, which is to slander.

clue.text: Indulge in 21, when yellow flower's beginning to come out

indicators.note: out signals the letter being removed from the flower's name

parts.note: the buttercup is a common yellow wild flower

indicators.note: the beginning of the word come, its first letter

explanation.surface: Lay on the compliments as a yellow bloom starts to open.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer at 21 across, sweet talk; 'out' takes C, the 'beginning to' 'come', from BUTTERCUP. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is to praise them insincerely to win favour, which is to lay on compliments.

clue.text: A ploy designed to cover commercial cargo

indicators.note: something designed is put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ad is a commercial on television

explanation.surface: A scheme devised to hide goods shipped for trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges A PLOY into PAYLO; 'to cover' is a loose link, and AD follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The payload is the part of a vehicle's load that earns revenue, the paying freight it carries.

clue.text: Takes off, having left out thanks for holiday

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for left is removed

parts.note: a plane flies when it takes off into the air
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a trip, having forgotten to say thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link; FLIES loses L, then TA follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive holiday, especially a religious one in Spain or Latin America.

clue.text: Cook, with milk as an ingredient, and butter

indicators.note: something added as an ingredient goes into the mixture, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is coffee made with lots of hot milk; the clue treats it as milk

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cook with milk added, then put in butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'butter' is the noun meaning smooth, insincere praise, not the dairy spread the cooking surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, butter can mean gross compliments or soft soap, the same thing as excessive praise.

clue.text: When young, radical had taken over university town in Finland

indicators.note: in a down clue, the radical sits over, above, the university letter

parts.note: a Young Turk is a young radical

explanation.surface: A youthful revolutionary seized a Finnish university town.
explanation.definitionFit: Turku is a city on the south-west coast of Finland, home to universities.

clue.text: Not about to disclose what the meat course may be

definitions.text: what the meat course may be

indicators.note: not about means without the word for about

parts.note: to reveal is to disclose
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A host refuses to say what the main course will be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is calf meat, one possible meat course at a meal.

clue.text: Behave as 17ac might, making moves — grin stupidly

indicators.note: doing something stupidly suggests the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dictator's behaviour, making manoeuvres with a silly grin.
explanation.walkthrough: '17ac' is the answer at 17 across, a tyrant; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant typically rules badly, which is to misgovern the country.

clue.text: All bar first and last parts of speech is in proportion

indicators.text: All bar first and last parts of
indicators.note: keep everything except the opening and closing letters of the word for speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Most of a talk sits in balance with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' is a link. The first and last letters, O and N, go from ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relation in size between two quantities, which is a proportion.

clue.text: Having had good training in spring, still unable to fly

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
an aircraft kept on the ground is grounded

explanation.surface: A fledgling that trained well in spring still cannot get airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'spring' is the water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoroughly schooled in the basics is said to be firmly founded in a subject.
